(1) CODE DERIVATION, core model section 3 pattern 1: data/wang_2026_efl_tam.py melts the S2 Appendix .xlsx's own columns BY NAME (SCALES['wang_2026_teaching_presence'] = [f'TP{i}' for i in range(1,9)]), so the IRW code IS the deposit column header -- no positional step, no rename. But the deposit column header is NOT the appendix item number (see 2), and the .xlsx carries no variable or value labels, so mapping_basis is reconstructed, not data_labels or paper_explicit. (2) THE RENUMBERING, and how it was settled. The S1 Appendix prints twelve TP items (TP1-TP12); the deposit has eight columns (TP1-TP8); the paper states 'low-factor-loading items (like TP3, TP4, TP5, and TP6) being removed' and its Table 2 lists exactly the other eight (TP1, TP10, TP11, TP12, TP2, TP7, TP8, TP9, in that alphabetical order). All eight deposit columns load 0.756-0.810 on their own first component, i.e. none is one of the sub-0.60 discards, so the deposit holds the retained eight renumbered 1-8. Which appendix item each deposit column is was proved from Table 2's VIF column: VIF is a per-item function of the construct correlation matrix, the method reproduces all 14 published VIFs of the four sibling constructs (ATT, PU, TA, BI) exactly to the printed digit, and on the live TP data it reproduces all eight published TP VIFs to within 0.0005 under the alphabetical assignment -- which is the unique best of 40320 permutations, the runner-up (a TP2/TP7 swap) being 0.011 worse. See verify_wang_2026_teaching_presence.R (VERDICT: PASS). (3) STEP 3b -- THE TABLE NAME IS WRONG. TP is technology perception, not teaching presence; the paper's abbreviation list and its section 3.3 heading both say so, and data/wang_2026_efl_tam.py records that it guessed the construct names from column prefixes without checking item text. Extraction is against what the live data is; instrument names the correct construct; the table name and the dictionary Description ('TAM teaching-presence scale') need correcting. (4) REVERSE CODING, an override of the printed anchors. Appendix TP2 and TP11 are negatively worded (the paper notes 'reverse-coded items (e.g., TP2) were included'; the upstream Khukalenko et al. 2022 table italicises the same positions as reverse-coded). In the deposit and in the live table their columns correlate +0.516..+0.595 with the other seven, so they are stored already reverse-scored. option_text for live TP3 and TP5 is therefore reversed (resp 1 = 'Strongly Agree' .. resp 5 = 'Strongly Disagree'); the other six items carry the appendix's printed order. Nothing was padded with its own number. (5) LANGUAGE / FALLBACK: administration was Chinese; the recoverability check covered every file in scope -- S1 Appendix .docx (all paragraphs and all table cells), S2 Appendix .xlsx (all three sheets) and the article text -- and all three contain ZERO CJK characters, so the study's own English ships in the base fields with the four _translated columns empty, language=Chinese, text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied. The upstream source the paper names is Khukalenko IS, Kaplan-Rakowski R, An Y, Iushina VD (2022), Educ Inf Technol 27:11591-11613, doi:10.1007/s10639-022-11061-0, open access in PMC9115738, whose Table 2 prints the same sixteen VR-classroom statements; the article states no fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause on the instrument -- only Springer's article copyright line, which is a term about the article, not the instrument (the PANAS case). Silence is permission, so it ships; per the standing rule a round may write only block rows, so no register row was added. public_note: This table was published until 2026-09-27 as wang_2026_teaching_presence; it is the study's TECHNOLOGY PERCEPTION (TP) construct -- teachers' judgements of digital games in the classroom -- and was renamed for that reason. Item and response wording is shown in English: Wang and Zou (2026) administered a Chinese translation and no Chinese wording appears anywhere in their deposit, so their own English from the S1 Appendix questionnaire ships in its place. The appendix numbers twelve TP items while the published data carry eight, because four were dropped for low loadings and the remainder were renumbered; the shipped text follows the renumbering that reproduces all eight of the paper's published Table 2 VIFs to within 0.0005 and is the unique best of 40320 possible assignments. Two of the eight items are negatively worded and are stored already reverse-scored (TP3 = 'Requires DG technological training, which takes too much time.', TP5 = 'Makes classroom management more difficult.'): for those two, and only those two, resp 1 means Strongly Agree and resp 5 means Strongly Disagree, which is how their option_text is shipped.
